For about 50 years, my mom has been hosting all of her children and grandchildren for Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. That's a long-standing tradition, and it means a lot to everyone involved. Now, my mom is getting too old to continue hosting, so she asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are four of us, and we've been rotating hosting duties. So far, each of us has hosted one holiday. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family has never been part of our Thanksgiving or Christmas Eve gatherings. They live all over the country, and we haven't been as close to them. However, this year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. Initially, it was just a sister's trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet up there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because she thinks it's a "once in a lifetime event," and I agree with her. Plus, I want to go too. As soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to see what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He told me that our oldest sister is going to be pissed and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that "Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to NYC" and went on about how sad mom will be that I'm doing this.
